Who we are

About Stripe

Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies - from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups - use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

About the team

The Government Relations & Public Affairs team represents Stripe to governments, regulators, industry partners, and broader stakeholder audiences. We help policymakers understand the businesses building on Stripe, and help Stripe understand the policy decisions that affect them. Our EU work sits at the intersection of financial services, technology and economic policy. The team works closely with Policy Strategy, Legal, Communications and regional product and go-to-market teams to translate Stripe’s experience and our users’ needs into effective policy engagement.

What you’ll do

We are looking for an EU Government Relations Manager to advance Stripe’s priorities in Brussels through effective advocacy and strong relationships with policymakers. You will bring deep expertise in either payments and financial services policy or technology policy, and use that expertise to influence EU legislative and regulatory debates that matter to Stripe and the businesses we serve.

This is an advocacy-led role: you will develop and execute engagement strategies, build relationships across the EU institutions, and make persuasive arguments for policies that help European businesses start, grow and compete. Working closely with Policy Strategy, Legal and business colleagues, you will turn Stripe’s policy positions into practical advocacy, exercising judgment about where, when and how to engage.

The position is based in Brussels and reports to the Head of EU Government Relations. Its primary focus is the EU, working closely with colleagues across EMEA and globally.

Responsibilities

  • Develop and execute EU advocacy strategies for an agreed portfolio of issues, setting clear objectives, identifying opportunities to shape the policy making process.
  • Build and maintain relationships across the EU institutions, developing a strong network of policymakers, officials and advisers.
  • Represent Stripe directly in policy discussions, making clear, persuasive arguments grounded in our business, our users’ experiences and the needs of Europe’s digital economy.  
  • Bring deep subject expertise to Stripe’s advocacy in either payments and financial services or technology policy, while building the knowledge needed to engage effectively across a broad waterfront of issues.
  • Work closely with Policy Strategy, Legal, Product and Go-To-Market colleagues to develop and refine advocacy positions, drawing on their expertise and ensuring our engagement reflects commercial and technical realities, and the needs of our users.
  • Build support for shared policy objectives through trade associations, industry coalitions and engagement with other companies and stakeholders.
  • Gather political and regulatory intelligence to guide advocacy decisions, keeping colleagues informed of material developments and recommending when and how Stripe should act.

Who you are

We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

Minimum requirements

  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in government relations, advocacy, public affairs or public policy, including direct experience of EU policymaking and engagement.
  • Deep expertise in either payments and financial services policy or technology policy. Expertise in both is not required.
  • A demonstrated track record of developing and delivering advocacy strategies and influencing legislative or regulatory debates.
  • Strong understanding of EU institutions, political dynamics and legislative processes, with experience building productive relationships with policymakers and officials.
  • Sound political judgment: the ability to identify what matters, assess opportunities to influence outcomes, and recommend a practical course of action.
  • Curiosity about unfamiliar products and policy issues, and the ability to build working knowledge beyond your area of specialism.
  • Excellent written and spoken English, including the ability to turn complex issues into clear, persuasive arguments and adapt them to different audiences.
  • Proven collaborator who is resourceful, detail-oriented, and able to work both independently and as part of a team.
  • Willingness to travel for meetings and events.
  • Passionate about Stripe’s mission of helping ambitious businesses grow and thrive.
  • Empathy, humility, and some comedy.

Preferred qualifications

  • Experience working in a high-growth, rapidly scaling environment.
  • Industry experience working in technology, payments, merchant or financial services.
  • A willingness to work with a diverse group of policy, regulatory, and product nerds who embrace Stripe’s policy issues, our users and each other.
  • Experience in the other policy domain: technology policy for a payments and financial services specialist, or payments and financial services policy for a technology specialist.
  • Knowledge of the business landscape and experience with relevant business associations in the EU.
  • Globally-minded and interested: while the focus will be on the EU and the wider EMEA region, given Stripe’s global presence, projects will inevitably become broader than that and the person will have to translate and explain what’s happening in the region to a global audience within Stripe.

Principal Solutions Engineer, US

US, remote first with NY office available · Full-time · Solutions · Reports to CPO

About DFNS

Finance is moving onchain. Stablecoins, tokenized deposits, securities and funds are changing how money and assets are issued, held and transferred. The destination is a financial system where any asset can be issued, moved and governed onchain with the controls regulated institutions require. That shift needs a new foundation. Just as core banking systems manage accounts and ledgers today, financial institutions need a platform to manage digital assets. DFNS is that platform. Today, we secure hundreds of billions of dollars in assets every month for more than 500 clients worldwide.

Why this role

Every deal we win in the Americas ends with the client’s engineers asking the same thing: show us how this runs in our environment. You are the person who answers, from the first architecture session through integration, deployment and the first production transaction. In year one you will design the integrations behind our largest accounts in the Americas, cut the time from signed contract to production and turn what you learn into the reference architectures, documentation and product feedback that make every deployment after it faster.

What you’ll do

  • Design integration architectures for banks, fintechs and enterprises across the Americas, across SaaS, hybrid and on-premise deployments.

  • Guide clients from signed contract to first production transaction, hands on with their engineers in code, configuration and testing.

  • Lead the technical side of sales cycles with Sales (demos, proofs of concept, security and architecture reviews with client CTOs and architects).

  • Troubleshoot in production when it matters, working with Engineering and Security to get to root cause and resolution.

  • Build reference architectures, integration guides and sample code so each client starts further ahead than the last.

  • Feed product insight back to Engineering and Product, with the evidence of what clients struggle with and why.

  • Set the practices the Solutions team runs on as it grows.

What you bring

Must-haves

  • A record of taking enterprise clients from contract to production as a solutions, integration or forward deployed engineer, in financial services or another regulated industry.

  • Engineering depth to write and review integration code (TypeScript or another modern language) and to read our APIs and SDKs like an engineer rather than a presenter.

  • Fluency in cloud architecture, APIs, authentication and key management, enough to design and defend an architecture with a bank’s architects.

  • Comfort running a room with CTOs and security teams, and the written clarity to leave them with a document they can act on.

  • Experience with security due diligence and the questions regulated clients ask (deployment models, key custody, audit trails, controls).

  • Authorization to work in the United States and the ability to travel to clients.

Nice-to-haves

  • Digital assets, custody, stablecoins or tokenization in production.

  • MPC, HSMs or secure enclaves.

  • Blockchain networks and smart contracts.

  • Spanish or Portuguese for the wider Americas.

How we work

We are a distributed company headquartered in Paris. Our teams work from Europe, the US and Asia, with offices in New York, Geneva, Dubai, Singapore, Hong Kong and São Paulo. We write decisions down so they survive time zones. We hold our own work to the standards our clients are held to. We hire people who can own an outcome end to end and we give them the room to do it.

What we offer

A competitive base salary set by role and location, a bonus or variable plan where the role carries one and stock options vesting over four years. Healthcare, flexible vacation, parental leave and a one-time home technology allowance, with travel expenses covered. A MacBook and the equipment you need to do your best work. Remote first, with an office if you want one.

Base salary range in the US: $150,000 to $250,000

Hiring process

We aim to complete the process in 2 weeks and we tell you where you stand after every step.

  • Intro call with Co-CEO (30 minutes).

  • Personality and cognitive assessments, completed on your own time (45 minutes).

  • A technical take-home exercise

  • Focus Interviews (about 2.5 hours): code review (45 minutes), architecture review (45 minutes), cross function (30 minutes) and security best practices (30 minutes).

  • Reference calls and background checks.

Equal opportunity

DFNS is an equal opportunity employer and considers every applicant based on ability and potential, regardless of race, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, age or any other characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation at any point in the process, tell us and we will arrange it.

About Ramp

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.

About the Role

Every approval request, receipt reminder, payment alert, and card notification Ramp sends has to reach the right person, on the right channel, at the right time. When it does, finance teams close faster and employees spend less time chasing tasks. When it doesn't, a missed message can mean a stalled approval, a late payment, or a flood of notifications nobody asked for.

Ramp's Communications Platform team builds the shared system that every product team uses to reach customers. It handles transactional messages across email, SMS, push, Slack, Microsoft Teams, and WhatsApp, including templating, delivery, retries, digesting, user preferences, and delivery monitoring. The team also supports the conversational experiences that let customers work with Ramp directly from the channels they already use.

We're looking for a backend engineer to own a core part of that platform. You'll take responsibility for an area such as message delivery and channel integrations, communication preferences, or platform reliability and scale, set its technical direction within the team, and keep it correct and dependable as message volume and the number of teams building on it grow. You'll work closely with product, design, and engineering partners across Ramp to make communications faster, more reliable, and easier for every team to build on.

What You'll Do

  • Own the design and evolution of a core part of Ramp's communications platform, from technical design through launch, monitoring, and iteration

  • Build and extend integrations with messaging channels and delivery providers, including email, SMS, push, and workplace chat tools such as Slack and Microsoft Teams

  • Design delivery workflows that are idempotent, retry safely, and confirm successful delivery, so customers reliably get the messages they need without duplicate sends

  • Build communication preferences and controls that let users and administrators decide what they receive and where

  • Make the platform simple and safe for other Ramp engineers to build on, with clear abstractions, strong defaults, and good developer tooling

  • Improve the reliability, performance, and observability of the platform as message volume grows

  • Drive technical direction for your area and raise the engineering bar through design reviews, code reviews, and mentorship

What You'll Need

  • Experience designing, building, and operating production backend systems, including APIs, data models, and asynchronous workflows

  • A track record of owning a system or product area end to end and shaping its technical direction over time

  • Strong system design judgment, especially around reliability, idempotency, and correctness in high-volume distributed systems

  • Product sense: you care about the experience of the people receiving each message, not just the ticket, and you balance speed with quality

  • Clear communication and a collaborative approach to technical decisions across product, design, and engineering

Nice to Haves

  • Experience building notification, messaging, or communications platforms

  • Experience integrating with messaging providers or channel APIs, such as Twilio, SendGrid, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or WhatsApp

  • Experience building internal platforms or shared services used by many engineering teams

  • Experience scaling high-volume, event-driven, or queue-based systems

Company Description

About us

Solflare is a Solana self-custody wallet that puts people in control of their digital assets. Around 4 million users control $20 billion in funds through our wallet.

What started as a team of 6 in 2020 building Solana's first wallet, has grown into a team of 150 worldwide. We’re remote-first, but if you happen to stop by in Zagreb, Croatia, or Belgrade or Novi Sad, Serbia, we have an office you can work from if that’s what you prefer. 

Wherever we work, we share the same goal: a Web3 wallet for everyone, with financial freedom in their hands.

Job Description

The role

We're looking for a Senior SEO Specialist to own and advance Solflare's organic search strategy across traditional search engines and AI-powered discovery platforms.

We already have a solid SEO foundation in place. Your role won't be to start from scratch, but to build on what's working, identify untapped opportunities, and take our organic visibility to the next level.

You'll work on a large-scale website with potentially millions of indexed or indexable pages, where technical SEO, content strategy, and smart prioritization can have a significant impact.

This is a hands-on, high-ownership role for someone who enjoys both strategic thinking and getting things done. You'll collaborate directly with experienced colleagues across Marketing, Product, and Engineering, with the autonomy to shape how we approach organic growth.

Core responsibilities:

  • Own and evolve our SEO strategy - Build on our existing foundation, identify growth opportunities, and translate them into a clear, actionable roadmap.
  • Drive organic search performance - Improve rankings, qualified organic traffic, and visibility for Solflare and its products across global markets.
  • Lead technical SEO initiatives - Identify and prioritize opportunities related to crawling, indexing, site architecture, internal linking, and performance across a large-scale website.
  • Optimize for traditional and AI-powered search - Develop approaches to improve Solflare's visibility in Google, AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, and other emerging discovery platforms.
  • Shape our content SEO strategy - Work with content creators and other stakeholders to ensure landing pages, product pages, and editorial content are built around search intent and measurable organic growth opportunities.
  • Strengthen off-page SEO - Identify and execute opportunities to improve domain authority, backlink quality, and competitive positioning.
  • Improve product discoverability - Support organic visibility for Solflare's browser extension and other relevant product discovery channels.
  • Measure what matters - Monitor performance, turn data into actionable insights, and continuously refine priorities based on impact.
  • Collaborate across teams - Partner with Marketing, Product, and Engineering to turn SEO opportunities into implemented improvements.

 

Qualifications

Requirements

  • 5+ years of hands-on SEO experience, with a track record of delivering measurable organic growth in competitive markets.
  • Experience owning or significantly contributing to SEO strategy, from identifying opportunities to executing and measuring results.
  • Strong understanding of technical SEO, including crawling, indexing, site architecture, internal linking, and large-scale website optimization.
  • Solid experience with on-page SEO, content optimization, off-page SEO, and link-building strategies.
  • Proficiency with tools such as Ahrefs, Google Search Console, and other SEO analytics and auditing platforms.
  • Familiarity with AI search optimization (AEO) and an interest in how search behavior and discovery are evolving.
  • A data-driven approach, with the ability to prioritize initiatives based on potential business impact.
  • Ability to work independently, challenge assumptions, and collaborate effectively.
  • Strong communication skills and professional proficiency in English.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience in crypto, Web3, fintech, or another highly competitive digital industry.
  • Experience optimizing websites with a large number of dynamically generated pages.
  • Experience with international or multilingual SEO.
  • Knowledge of app store optimization (ASO) or Chrome Web Store discoverability.

 

Additional Information

You might not like it here…

But you might love it. Working at Solflare comes with trade-offs, and we’re open about them.

Crypto moves fast, and our priorities can shift with it. We launch new features and rethink existing projects as our users’ needs evolve, in bull and bear markets alike. That means a project you expected to work on may give way to a more pressing priority. We understand this can be energizing if you can adapt and reset as you go, and frustrating if you prefer long-term predictability.

We also highly rate how people work together. Yes, individual work matters, but so does helping others succeed. We share responsibility for the outcome, and we share credit for the wins.

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions.
 
Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out.
 
You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries.
  • Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline.
  • Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release.
  • Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision.
  • Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers.
  • Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product.
  • Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team.
  • Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee.
  • Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads.
  • Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records.

What We Look For In You  

  • 7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team.
  • Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required.
  • Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output.
  • Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting.
  • Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus.
  • Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle.
  • Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee.
  • Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines.

Nice to Haves

  • Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting.
  • Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale.
  • Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments.
  • Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.
  • Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit.

About Open Standard

Open Standard is building internet-native money. Data moved to the cloud, and dollars will move onchain. When they do, stablecoins become core financial infrastructure.

Our stablecoin, Open USD (OUSD), is built for that shift. Minting and redeeming are free at any volume. Nearly all reserve revenue goes back to the businesses that grow adoption. The partners who use OUSD govern it, rather than a single issuer.

OUSD is live on Base, Ethereum, Solana, and Tempo. Our founding partners are Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe, and Visa, and more than 200 banks, payment networks, fintechs, and crypto companies have signed up to use OUSD. Our CEO is Zach Abrams, who co-founded Bridge (acquired by Stripe for $1.1B) and previously led product at Brex, Coinbase, and Square.

OS is currently a team of about ten. We have a real shot at being the next inevitable transformation in stablecoins. We're hiring someone to help make us inevitable.

The role

We're hiring a Deputy General Counsel to help build the legal function at Open Standard alongside our General Counsel, a Founding Team member of Open Standard, who was also part of the founding team of Bridge. You'll be a partner to the GC, not a direct report in the usual sense. The two of you will divide the work by comparative advantage, and you'll own your areas end to end. We are AI-centric, highly scaled, and don't plan on building a large legal team for the foreseeable future. You'll do the work yourself, with AI agents and a tight group of outside counsel extending your reach.

Legal sits at the center of OS's business. You'll be integrated into OUSD design choices, partner deals, and launch decisions, all of which present needle moving commercial opportunities that depend on thoughtful legal decision making that unlocks value for the business.

What you'll do

  • Shape the product with our product and engineering teams: mint and redemption flows, partner rewards, wallet and chain integrations, and new use cases from cross-border payments to agentic commerce.

  • Structure and negotiate the deals OUSD runs on: network partner agreements, reserve and custody relationships, exchange and liquidity arrangements, and agreements with chains and protocols.

  • Work directly with the world's largest banks, card networks, and asset managers, answering their diligence, risk, and regulatory questions with credibility.

  • Find the creative structure when the easy answer is "no": the deal term, product change, or regulatory path that gets a partner live.

  • Help steward a new kind of governance model, with a company owned and governed by the partners who use its product.

  • Support our Head of Policy on regulator and policymaker engagement, comment letters, and industry work.

  • Assist with regulatory strategy for OUSD under the GENIUS Act and state and international regimes. This covers licensing paths, issuer and reserve arrangements, and how rewards and distribution are treated.

  • Build an AI-native legal function, using agents and workflows for contract review, diligence questionnaires, regulatory tracking, and partner questions.

  • Manage outside counsel in the US and abroad tightly, and know when not to use them.

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have 10+ years of legal experience, including substantial in-house time at crypto companies.

  • Know the stablecoin market cold from three angles: commercial, regulatory, and product. You can explain how issuers make money, how reserves and redemption work, what GENIUS changes, and where the market is going next.

  • Have worked with or inside large financial institutions and understand how banks, card networks, and asset managers make decisions. You earn their trust without starting to act like them.

  • Have creative commercial instincts and use them to shape deals and products, not just paper them. You're a regulatory and product lawyer who structures deals, not a contracts specialist who knows crypto.

  • Are scrappy and do the work yourself, from the first draft to the board memo.

  • Already use AI seriously in your practice, and have built agents or workflows that expand what one lawyer can do.

  • Write clearly and precisely, because most decisions here start in writing.

  • Are admitted to practice in a US jurisdiction.

Strong candidates may also have

  • Worked in-house at a stablecoin issuer

  • Worked in a bank's digital assets group, alongside crypto-native experience

  • Worked on stablecoin or payments licensing: trust charters, state money transmission, or non-US regimes such as MiCA

  • Helped build the legal function at an early-stage company

  • Relationships with regulators, policymakers, or industry groups in payments and digital assets
